# Working on herdr-orchestrators

This repo builds two ODD orchestrator agents, `hcorc` (Herdr desktop) and
`herdorc` (herdr terminal multiplexer), plus ten role agents, for several
coding CLIs. `README.md` describes the product; this file is for changing it.

## Sources and generated files

- Sources: `shared/` (core, docs, roles, skills, vendored herdr skill,
  `bin/orc.py`, `bin/guard.py`), `layers/` (per-orchestrator layers, shared
  section, slash-command templates), `mods/` (Claude Code-only plugins),
  `herdr-app/mods/` (Herdr desktop mods, for any CLI).
- Everything under `.claude/agents/`, `.claude/commands/` and every CLI's
  install location is generated by `install.py`. It writes the files into
  `dist/` (git-ignored; `$ORC_DIST` overrides it) and links each install
  location to them. Never edit generated files, nor the files behind the
  links; edit the source and regenerate. Shared files (`settings.json`
  hooks, Herdr layouts and `keys.json`, herdr's `config.toml`) are merged,
  never linked.
- Installing is `./install.sh` (every part the machine has) or
  `installers/<target>.sh` (one part). They are thin wrappers: the logic
  stays in `install.py` and `herdr-app/extras.py`. A new install option goes
  there, then into the wrapper's help and the README table.
- `shared/core`, `shared/docs`, `shared/roles` and most of `shared/skills`
  are ported from tomidev-shell by `scripts/port-*.py`, with every change
  recorded in `shared/PROVENANCE-*.md`. Change a ported text through its
  port script, so the provenance stays true. That includes `roles.json`:
  `port-roles.py` writes it whole (a role's `model` comes from its `MODELS`).
  The ported core and docs use the neutral terms too; a CLI-specific line
  goes in a conditional block of the core, never in a doc read at runtime.
- `herdr-app/patches/agent-flow/` patches the third-party Herdr app mod
  herdr-agent-flow so it draws `orc.py ensure --handoff` as a message. Its
  README names the agent-flow commit the patches are made against and how to
  reapply them after agent-flow is updated. Changing what `orc.py ensure`
  accepts (`--as`, `--name`, `--handoff`) needs the same change in the patch.

## Rules

- Keep prompts CLI-agnostic: say "ask tool", "subagent tool", "shell tool".
  `install.py` (`VOCAB`, `CLIS`) maps them per CLI. Put anything that only
  works where a CLI has the phase hook, the guard or commands in
  `<!-- if:hooks -->`, `<!-- if:guard -->` or `<!-- if:commands -->` blocks.
  Only the mods in `mods/` may be specific to Claude Code.
- Parity: every CLI gets the commands and the guard. `install.py` writes the
  commands as user-only skills where a CLI has no command files
  (`SKILL_COMMAND_CLIS`, identical text for each, so a shared skills folder
  holds one copy) and registers `guard.py --format <cli>` in each CLI's hook
  format (`merged_hooks`, OpenCode's plugin `opencode_plugin()`, Grok's hooks
  file `grok_hooks()`, pi's extension `pi_guard()`; pi's commands are prompt
  templates). A new CLI gets both, or the README says why not. Never narrow an
  orchestrator's tools: only agy needs a `tools` list (`AGY_TOOLS`, agy's own
  names), since an agy agent without one gets read-only tools. `guard.py` reads each format's input
  in `command_of` and answers in `answer`; where a hook can only refuse
  (codex, opencode) an ask-class call is refused with the `ORC_CONFIRMED=1`
  rerun instruction. pi's extension shows an ask-class call in pi's dialog.
- Outside Claude Code the guard knows the orchestrator from
  `orc_state.record_lead` (`orc.py --as`) and `lead_of_session`. Where a CLI
  keeps one process across conversations (pi: `/new`, `/resume`), the record
  is per conversation: `record_lead` reads it from `SESSION_VARS`
  (`PI_SESSION_ID`) and the hook sends it as `session_id`. Tests that run
  `orc.py --as` set `ORC_LEADS` to a temp file.
- `orc.py` identifies the orchestrator from `--as <agent>` or
  `$CLAUDE_CODE_AGENT`. The mods read its files, so keep these stable:
  the phase file name and its `phase` key (`orc-cache`), the herdorc state
  file (one per lead pane: `herdorc-<session>-<workspace>.pane-<lead>.json`,
  so two herdorc in one workspace each control only the panes they created),
  and `~/.local/state/orc/reports` (`orc-graph`).
- `mods/orc-graph/hooks/roster.ts` and `mods/orc-context/hooks/roster.ts`
  duplicate `ROLES`, the role-name pattern, the herdorc state file path,
  `safe()` and the pane ownership rule (id, label, terminal) from `orc.py` /
  `orc_state.py`. A change there needs the same change in both copies.
- Commands are read as shell words in four places, each a copy for a reason
  (a mod or plugin installs alone): `shared/bin/guard.py`; `shellCommands` and
  `program` in `mods/orc-graph/hooks/graph.ts`, copied into
  `mods/orc-cache/hooks/cache.ts`; and `commands`/`calls` in
  `herdr/plugins/orc-flow/lib/scan.cjs`, copied into
  `herdr-app/patches/agent-flow/orc-handoff.patch`. A fix in one copy goes to
  its twin. They agree that an option's value is never a target and that
  `orc.py ensure` hands off only with `--launch` and `--handoff` (or
  `--prompt-file`). The graphs use the pane name in ensure's JSON answer once
  `prompt_sent` or `prompt_delivered_at_launch` confirms delivery.
- The Claude Code mods' panes are opt-in: `/orc-graph` and `/orc-context` open
  them, their `openPane` option opens them at session start. Never open a pane
  unasked. Bump a mod's `version` when its behaviour changes, so
  `install.py`'s `plugin update` picks it up.
- `herdr-app/mods/orc-skills` reads `orc.py skills --json`; keep its `conflicts`
  and `skills` keys stable. Run `herdr-app check herdr-app/mods/orc-skills`
  after changing it; `seen.js` (which conflicts a toast reported) is pure, and
  `tests/test_skills.sh` imports it. A new module of the mod goes in
  `herdr_mod_files`. Its layout node IDs (`orc-skills-bar`, `-toggle`,
  `-panel`, and the `tabs-row` column around the bar, which a tab bar that
  grows taller resizes) are shared with `install.py`; never edit Herdr's
  shipped layouts or mods (clone them). The manifest's `tabs_row` says whether
  the install made that column (uninstall removes only its own). Herdr's file
  watcher doesn't look through a mod folder's link, so `herdr_place` and
  `extras.py` make the link again whenever a build changes: that is what
  reloads the mod.
- `herdr-app/mods/orc-panes` becomes the layout's pane header and draws
  through a copy of the header it replaced: `panes_files` copies that mod's
  modules under `base/` at install, and `props.replaces` keeps it for
  `panes_release`. `panes_take` takes only the headers drawn by that same mod,
  so a layout that mixes headers keeps the others. Its labels `orc.pane-name`
  and `orc.phase` (`names.js`) are shared with `orc.py` (`PHASE_LABEL`,
  `HcBackend.set_label`): change both
  together. `extras.py` gives the header back around a mod's own installer or
  uninstaller (`panes_hand_back`, `panes_take_back`). The repo folder has no
  `base/`, so run `herdr-app check` on a build (the installed
  `mods/orc-panes`, or one made with `panes_files`).
- Tests and experiments never touch the user's terminals or sessions: use
  `HC_SESSION=<name>` for herdr-core and a named `herdr --session` for herdr.
- `herdr/plugins/orc-flow/` is a herdr plugin (Node, any CLI), ported from
  herdr-agent-flow (MIT; its licence is the plugin's `LICENSE`, its changes
  are listed in the plugin's README). It reads herdorc's state file and
  copies `ROLES` and the state file path rule from `shared/roles/roles.json`
  and `shared/bin/orc_state.py` into `lib/herdr.mjs`: a change there needs
  the same change in the plugin. It also reads `orc.py ensure ... --handoff`,
  the herdr commands herdorc's layer uses to prompt and read role panes, and
  report files named `<pane-name>-<task>.md`; keep them in step with
  `layers/herdorc.md`. `orc.py flow` opens the plugin's `graph` pane the
  way its `bin/open.sh` does (entrypoint, `ORC_FLOW_PLACEMENT`,
  `ORC_FLOW_ORIGIN`), beside the orchestrator's pane; for hcorc it splits the
  agent-flow Herdr app mod. A change to either side needs the other.
- `herdr-app/extras.json` pins each third-party Herdr app mod to a commit
  whose code was read. Bump a `ref` only after reading the new code, and
  check that `herdr-app/patches/agent-flow` still applies to a new agent-flow.
  Tests use `ORC_EXTRAS_SPEC` and `ORC_EXTRAS_SRC`, never the network.
- `herdr plugin link` writes to herdr's config, which every herdr session
  shares. Link the plugin for tests only in a herdr whose config is isolated
  (`XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<short dir>`, since herdr's socket path must stay short),
  with a named session.

## Commands

- Regenerate this repo's `.claude/`: `python3 scripts/build-agents.py`
- Install: `./install.sh --help`, `installers/<target>.sh --help`,
  `python3 install.py --help`
- Tests: `bash tests/test_install.sh`, `bash tests/test_skills.sh`,
  `bash tests/test_runtime.sh` (self-contained), then
  `bash tests/test_guard.sh`, `bash tests/test_orc_herdr.sh`,
  `bash tests/test_orc_hc.sh` (need herdr / Herdr desktop).
- Claude Code mods: `claude plugin validate mods/<mod>`,
  `claude plugin test mods/<mod>`.
- herdr skill drift: `python3 scripts/sync-herdr-skill.py`
- orc-flow plugin tests: `node --test herdr/plugins/orc-flow/test/`
